subject: GPU pool split-brain: incident notification, interim mitigations, and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@aurora-ai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: [Redwood] Immediate: GPU pool split-brain detected in us-west-2 (Aurora AI dedicated pool)

Alex —

We detected a condition this morning (10:01 PDT) where two control-plane replicas momentarily believed they owned the same dedicated GPU pool in your us-west-2 reservation. That "split-brain" led to the autoscaler making conflicting allocation decisions, which in turn caused a short burst of preemptions and significant tail latency for a subset of your requests between ~09:58–10:10 PDT.

What we’ve done so far (interim mitigations):
- Isolated the affected pool and diverted new allocation requests to warm standby capacity to prevent further evictions.
- Disabled cross-controller leader election for the impacted shard and forced a single leader to reestablish consistent ownership.
- Enabled conservative autoscaler thresholds while we perform a deeper diagnostic to avoid oscillation.

Impact (so far):
- Elevated error rate and 95th/99th token latency for ~7% of requests during the window noted above.
- We saw multiple request restarts for jobs that were using KV cache; no customer data was exposed.

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether you saw application-level errors or queue build-up on your side during 09:55–10:15 PDT? If you have an ops contact we should include on the postmortem call, please loop them in.

We'll schedule a quick sync in the next hour; in the meantime Marcus is collecting allocator logs and a timeline. I’ll follow up with a proposed remediation timeline and credit proposal after we complete the first triage.

Apologies for the disruption — we know predictability is critical.

— Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (CSV timeline of events)]
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@aurora-ai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@aurora-ai.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Immediate: GPU pool split-brain detected in us-west-2 (Aurora AI dedicated pool)

Karthik —

Thanks for the heads up. We did see a spike in inference errors and a corresponding backlog in our request queue; it caused some retries on the worker side. No data corruption that we can see, but the customer-facing latency increase impacted a few SLAs during that 15-minute window.

We need an ETA on a full fix and clarification on how you’ll prevent this from recurring. Also please include a proposed customer credit for the SLA miss. We’re available for a 30‑minute call at 11:00 PDT.

— Alex
Head of Platform Ops, Aurora AI
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@aurora-ai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Immediate: GPU pool split-brain detected in us-west-2 (Aurora AI dedicated pool) — interim RCA and mitigation plan

Alex —

Quick technical summary from triage:
- Root cause: a transient networking partition between controller replicas combined with a race in our allocator leader election. Two controllers accepted allocation leases for overlapping subsets of the same pool for ~70s.
- Effect: concurrent allocation attempts caused premature eviction of warm instances on one side and delayed KV cache population on the other, producing the latency/errors you observed.

Short-term mitigations completed:
- We forced a single controller leader for the shard, drained inflight allocations, and prevented any further dual-ownership events.
- Conservatively increased the autoscaler hysteresis windows and disabled speculative eviction heuristics for your pool.
- We captured allocator logs and the state dump (attached snippets) for forensic analysis.

Proposed timeline for roll-forward fixes (subject to change as we complete validation):
- 10/15: apply patch to leader-election backoff to include an explicit quorum confirmation step (non-disruptive unit/integration tests first).
- 10/16: progressive rollout to controller fleet in us-west-2 with canary → ramp → full; monitor for eviction and latency regressions.
- 10/17–10/20: post-deployment soak, then roll change globally if stable.

Customer credit proposal: one-time credit equal to two days of Dedicated pool usage for the affected reservation; we will calculate the exact amount and include it in the final postmortem.

I’ve attached: allocator-log-snippet.txt and pool-ownership-dag.png showing the conflicting ownership windows.

Let us know if the 11:00 PDT slot works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

— Marcus
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

[Attachments: allocator-log-snippet.txt, pool-ownership-dag.png]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@aurora-ai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Final incident summary and follow-up actions — INF-4129

Alex —

Thanks again for the quick sync on Thursday. This note consolidates the final findings, actions we’ve taken, and next steps. Please consider this our formal post-incident communication for INF-4129.

Summary of impact:
- Window: 2026-10-14T09:58–2026-10-14T10:10 PDT.
- Customers affected: subset of traffic on Aurora AI’s dedicated pool in us-west-2 (~7% of requests routed to the impacted shard).
- User impact: increased 95th/99th token latency and ~3% request error rate during the window; retries mitigated some failures but you correctly observed backlog pressure.

Root cause (final):
- A transient network partition between controller replicas combined with insufficient quorum verification in our allocator leader-election path allowed two controllers to independently assume ownership of overlapping partitions for ~70s.

Remediation performed (completed):
- Forced leader reconciliation and prevented further dual-ownership events.
- Rolled a hotfix to require explicit quorum verification during leader acquisition (deployed to canary on 2026-10-15; full rollout completed 2026-10-16 04:20 PDT).
- Autoscaler default hysteresis increased for affected pools; speculative eviction heuristics disabled until further stability validated.
- Added automated alerts to detect overlapping lease assignments and trigger an immediate safe-failover policy.

Long-term action items (tracking):
- INF-4210: Improve controller networking observability and add conservative backoff to election under partial partition conditions.
- INF-4211: Add deterministic post-failover KV-cache rehydration to reduce request restarts and tail latency.
- INF-4212: Add a customer-facing SLA dashboard widget for pool ownership and leader events.

Credits and customer remediation: per our proposal we will issue a one-time credit equal to two days of your Dedicated reservation usage. Finance will mail a formal credit memo by 2026-10-18.

Attached are the forensic artifacts and the incident timeline export for your records. If you’d like a deeper technical walkthrough for your SREs, Marcus and I can schedule a follow-up next week.

We’re sorry for the disruption and appreciate your partnership while we tightened the leader-election safety properties.

— Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: incident-timeline.csv, pool-ownership-dag.png, allocator-log-snippet.txt]
